children: Despite Thursday morning's pre-market stock selloff, fueled by renewed AI spending worries after mixed earnings from Tesla and Meta Platforms, an Asian selloff, and a sharp jump in oil on Middle East headlines, I still think a year-end rally is in the cards. This looks more like a digestion of recent gains than the start of a deeper breakdown, with seasonality remaining supportive for the rest of the year.

On the oil side, Brent is climbing toward the $112 area, but could be approaching a top amid headline fatigue. Oil flows through and around the Strait of Hormuz have rebounded strongly and are running above prewar levels in aggregate, highlighting how effectively the market has adapted even as attacks continue.

Touching on the Kospi's sharp recent swings, falling more than 3% on Thursday after a similar-sized rebound the day before, and sitting well below mid-year highs, raises the possibility that the Korean stock index is in the process of bottoming. Heavy concentration in Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix has left it especially exposed to the global AI spending scare. The benchmark is now more than 40% below its 52-week high, but a sustained turn higher from here would matter well beyond Seoul. The index acts as an indicator for the broader semiconductor and AI complex, and stabilization would signal that the worst of the risk-off washout in the tech trade may be behind us, improving the odds of a broader year-end rally.

I use technical analysis. Turning to the weekly chart on a three-year time frame, the KOSPI Index is testing critical support as price action pulls back into a prior bull flag breakout zone directly above the very round 5000 level. This key floor coincides with the long bullish hammer from the week ending July 31, which closed more than 1,300 points off its intraweek low to terminate a severe seven-week losing streak. Although the benchmark has remarkably failed to register back-to-back weekly gains throughout the second half of 2026, holding above the 5000 area maintains an exceptionally favorable risk/reward profile into year-end.

While bears argue that declining volume since early July reflects a lack of capitulation, underlying momentum indicators suggest selling pressure is exhausting itself at key support instead. The weekly Relative Strength Index has compressed into the oversold 30 region, a key momentum zone that has consistently triggered technical mean-reversion bounces in prior cycles. If the 5250 level does give way all bullish thoughts are negated.

Furthermore, concerns that extreme RSI readings render the index vulnerable to prolonged selling ignore the KOSPI's recent structural behavior. During its explosive 200% rally between mid-2025 and mid-2026, the index proved that momentum can remain overbought for extended periods, holding well above the overbought 70 threshold throughout that entire advance.
The Kospi closed at 5533.76 on Thursday.

Turning to the Brent crude daily chart, several technical signatures point to potential topping behavior at current levels. Primary among these is a prominent bearish RSI divergence, where price action registered higher highs across September and October while the RSI printed a lower high, failing to confirm upward momentum. This non-confirmation serves as a classic technical warning that the prevailing uptrend is losing steam and momentum.

As price approaches the $115 handle, overhead technical headwinds become increasingly formidable. This resistance zone coincides with the upper boundary of a bearish rising wedge originating in June. The initial July pullback to the $70 floor successfully filled the late-February gap stemming from the outbreak of the Iran conflict. Furthermore, this retest confronts the breakdown level of a prior bull-flag formation, marked by Brent's 10% gap-down on May 25.

These converging resistance levels reinforce the case for a major double top, anchored by the massive long-legged doji printed on March 9, a volatile session that carved out an extraordinary $35 intraday range.
Brent Crude was trading around $111 Thursday.

Doug Busch is the senior technical analyst at Barron's Investor Circle. His technical view is added to stock picks, including those published exclusively for Investor Circle readers. A glossary of technical terms is updated regularly with new entries.
